metadata.case_name: LAI PING WAH v. CHINA INSURANCE CO. LTD. AND ANOTEHR

injuries.icd_description: Laceration without foreign body of head

source: Right forehead numbness throughout the whole day and reduced sensation over right forehead.
injuries.icd_description: Laceration without foreign body of head

injuries.description: Left leg laceration - (this was also recorded in a diagram as 7 cm deep to muscle).
source: Left leg laceration - (this was also recorded in a diagram as 7 cm deep to muscle).
The operation record of 11th September deals with the wound to the left calf region.
injuries.icd_description: Laceration without foreign body of lower leg

injuries.description: Fracture of the left inferior pubic ramus
source: The discharge/transfer summary dated 26th October, some six weeks or so after the accident, refers to a fracture of the left inferior pubic ramus
injuries.icd_description: Fracture of pubis without disruption of pelvic ring

injuries.description: Fracture of the right little toe
source: The discharge/transfer summary dated 26th October, some six weeks or so after the accident, refers to a fracture of ... the right little toe

injuries.description: Optic neuritis (left optic neuritis / Optical neuritis leading to idiopathy or secondary demyelinating disease)
source: MR1 scan of orbit on 25th May 1996 showed abnormal enhancement of left optic nerve.
"Optical neuritis leading to idiopathy or secondary demyelinating disease (multiplesclerosis)."
She became totally blind in or about March 1996
Total blindness of left eye. "Can't even detect light."
injuries.icd_description: Other specified injury of eye or orbit

injuries.body_part: central nervous system / spinal cord and optic nerves
source: Either the injuries themselves or the contamination, or the necessary tetanus toxoid injections, collectively or individually, led to the development of Devic's Syndrome - and I accept Dr. Huang's view that this was probably a case of Devic's, independent of Multiple Sclerosis.
Paraplegia had set in from about May 1996 onwards and further deterioration led to tetraplegia.
injuries.icd_description: Injury of cervical spinal cord, unspecified

injuries.description: Diagnosis recorded as multiple sclerosis (recorded variably in medical notes)
source: Her diagnosis has been variously recorded as multiple sclerosis, Devic's Syndrome and other forms of demyelinating disease
The discharge summary diagnosing multiple sclerosis

manifestations.description: Back pain with tenderness T6 to T8 region.
Left leg laceration (8 cm deep to muscle).
Forehead numbness / reduced sensation over right forehead / hypersensitivity of the scalp above the scar, exaggerated by touching
Dizziness (transient and mild on several occasions)
Progressive reduction of left eye vision leading to total blindness of left eye
Deterioration in vision in her right eye leading to total blindness
Progressive weakness in her legs requiring her to use a frame to walk
Bilateral lower limb twitching and weakness
Intermittent pain over the right parietal region with numbness and paraesthesiae over the right upper face and occasional tinnitus
Reduced power in her lower limbs and she was chair bound / wheelchair bound
Right foot-drop / clumsiness of the right leg (reported)

treatments_received: Removal of glass beads under LA on multiple occasions
Bone scan (booked / to be carried out on 3rd October)
CT scan (admitted for CT scan noted 25th April)
MRIs of orbit, brain and spine (multiple dates)
Debridement and drainage for infection on 7th October

losses.description: Permanent cosmetic disfigurement from facial lacerations which required suturing.
Loss of sight: progressive optic neuritis leading to total blindness (left eye by April 1995; totally blind in or about March 1996).
Progressive weakness leading to use of walking frame, then paraplegia and ultimately quadriplegia / wheelchair bound.
Dependency on others, continuous decline and need for assistance with daily activities as condition worsened to wheelchair bound and quadriplegia.
Permanent impairment from multiple injuries including leg lacerations and fractures and subsequent neurological disease.

losses.category: Loss of ability to do domestic tasks
losses.description: Loss of ability to perform ordinary household activities due to progressive neurological decline and paralysis.
Severe decline, dependency and disability would have reduced ability to participate in social interaction and activities.
